name: Bow and Arrow Choke from Invisible Collar
description: Bow and Arrow Choke from Invisible Collar requires a separate back take. The gi collar grip and rear body control are absent from the facing high guard.
submission_type: Gi collar choke from rear control
summary: The Bow and Arrow Choke is a gi collar choke from rear control, using a collar grip and lower-body counter-control to create tension across the neck as the attacker changes angle.
overview:
The attacker has rear torso access, a secure jacket-collar grip and control of the opponent's lower body. Invisible Collar is a facing rubber-guard clinch without a required jacket grip. Rear control and a real collar grip must be established separately; this finish does not have a clothing-free equivalent with the same grip.

Keep the torso connected from behind before reaching for the collar. Place the hand securely in the jacket collar without dragging the cloth across the face. Use the available leg or trouser control to manage the opponent's hips. Turn the body gradually to create opposing collar and lower-body tension.

Use a sound gi and gradual tension. Do not substitute face pressure, jerk the collar, or treat a chin tuck as reliable protection from a secured choke.

Instructional sources: [Stephan Kesting and Emily Kwok — bow-and-arrow choke and escape](https://www.grapplearts.com/bow-arrow-choke-escape/); [Eddie Bravo — MTS 134 Invisible Collar in Austin](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KCyIwacRKu8).

defender.name: from Invisible Collar Defender
defender.description: Bow and Arrow Choke from Invisible Collar (defender): Hand fight before the attacker obtains a deep grip from behind. Avoid giving the attacker a large sideways angle while the collar remains fixed.
defender.overview:
The attacker has rear torso access, a secure jacket-collar grip and control of the opponent's lower body. Invisible Collar is a facing rubber-guard clinch without a required jacket grip. Rear control and a real collar grip must be established separately; this finish does not have a clothing-free equivalent with the same grip.

Hand fight before the attacker obtains a deep grip from behind. Avoid giving the attacker a large sideways angle while the collar remains fixed. Use an early downward body adjustment only while the neck has space and the grip is not loaded.

Work at the elbow lever while protecting the neck instead of merely tugging at the sleeve. Stop when the choke is established; do not attempt a violent turn against a fixed collar. Recover facing position only when the neck and collar have been released.

Use a sound gi and gradual tension. Do not substitute face pressure, jerk the collar, or treat a chin tuck as reliable protection from a secured choke.

After breaking the collar connection and freeing the trapped head, bring a shoulder to the mat and move the hips toward facing guard. A short hip escape can recover a knee once the rear attachment opens; it must not pull the neck against a grip that is still closed.
